```sql
WITH agg AS (
    SELECT pv.product_id,
           count(DISTINCT o.id)        AS order_count,
           sum(ol.quantity)            AS quantity,
           sum(ol.line_total_cents)    AS revenue_cents,
           count(DISTINCT pv.id)       AS variant_count
      FROM orders o
      JOIN order_lines ol      ON ol.order_id = o.id
      JOIN product_variants pv ON pv.id = ol.variant_id::uuid
     WHERE o.tenant_id = %(tenant_id)s
       AND o.created_at >= %(from)s
       AND o.created_at <  %(to)s
       AND o.status IN ('paid', 'processing', 'shipped', 'delivered')
     GROUP BY pv.product_id
     ORDER BY quantity DESC, revenue_cents DESC
     LIMIT %(limit)s
)
SELECT p.id,
       p.sku,
       p.name,
       p.brand,
       p.currency,
       a.order_count,
       a.quantity,
       a.revenue_cents,
       a.variant_count
  FROM agg a
  JOIN products p ON p.id = a.product_id
 ORDER BY a.quantity DESC, a.revenue_cents DESC
```

De aggregatie groepeert nu alleen op `pv.product_id` in plaats van op vijf brede productkolommen. Dat mag, omdat `products.id` de primaire sleutel is en de foreign key garandeert dat elk product bestaat. Daardoor worden sortering, `LIMIT` en de `count(DISTINCT)`-bewerkingen op smalle rijen uitgevoerd, en worden `products` pas daarna voor alleen de top-N rijen via de primaire-sleutelindex opgehaald.
